transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get this pre-air lock meeting started. We've got the finale going live Saturday at 9 PM Eastern, and we need to finalize the voting package today so everything is documented before transmission. We've got standards, platform production, rights, and data protection all represented here. Let's walk through the current draft: voting is open to our broadcast audience via SMS and the online portal. Before I make the final binding decision, I want to hear from each of you on your areas. What issues or concerns do we need to address?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something from the standards side. After the draft voting rules were circulated, I issued the network's current standards memo, which establishes three binding requirements: voters must be at least 13 years old, each voter may cast exactly one vote per verified account, and voting must close at 9:50 PM Eastern. The current draft doesn't yet reflect these requirements, so we need to make sure the final package incorporates all three before transmission.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue from platform production. I completed the platform certification test this morning, and the SMS integration failed certification — only the web portal passed. Additionally, the approved portal requires account verification before a vote is accepted. This means we cannot offer SMS voting as things currently stand, and the portal's account verification requirement needs to be reflected in the final package.
transcript.speaker: A3

I obtained the finalist label's written approval today, and it confirms that the voting interface may display finalist names and approved headshots, but may NOT use any finalist performance audio or video. The current draft interface still contains performance clips, so those need to be removed before the final package is locked.

transcript.text: I need to flag two data protection issues from my privacy review with the voting vendor this week. First, the review limits participation to viewers physically located in the United States and Canada, but the current draft still describes worldwide participation. Second, the review requires voter identifiers to be deleted within 30 days, but the current draft has no deletion step at all. Both of these need to be incorporated into the final package before transmission.
